title: PSYCH-GPT: Alignment between natural language processing and large language models in psychiatric disorders
summary:
Background: Disorders such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, depression, and schizophrenia are often associated with differences in how affected individuals process language. At the same time, artificial intelligence systems have emerged that compute language in ways that resemble the human brain.
Research question: We investigate whether and to what extent this similarity between the brain and artificial intelligence is altered in people with these disorders.
Methodology: Participants listen to short German spoken texts inside a magnetic resonance imaging scanner while their brain activity is recorded. These activity patterns are then compared to the internal computations of various artificial intelligence language programs. Four groups are examined: individuals with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, depression, schizophrenia, and healthy controls (30 participants each).

interventions.name: All participants undergo the same examination protocol: digital screening and informed consent (approx. 7 min.), neuropsychological tests and clinical interviews (approx. 90 min.), and a functional MRI session (approx. 60–90 min.) at 3 Tesla. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Native-level German language proficiency
Capacity to consent
No contraindications for MRI
For patient groups additionally: confirmed diagnosis of ADHD, depression, or schizophrenia (clinically documented); stable medication for at least 2 weeks; for depression: at least moderate severity
Exclusion criteria:
MRI-relevant metal implants (especially pacemakers, prostheses, non-MRI-compatible intrauterine devices)
Fresh, large-area, or metal-containing tattoos; any tattoos in the head or neck region
Acute psychotic or manic episode; acute suicidality; acute substance-related intoxication or withdrawal
Severe neurological disorders
Significant hearing impairment
For healthy controls additionally: existing psychiatric disorder
For patient groups additionally: severe psychiatric comorbidity beyond the primary diagnosis
